This runtime import hardcodes tag `31` at build time and bypasses the whole version-gating mechanism in this file. Because the `ActivityComponent` entry is **not** included in the `const {...} = ReactTypeOfWork` destructuring (lines 554-581 and 902-928), both `case ActivityComponent:` sites (lines 631 and 1491) resolve to this imported constant instead of the per-version value. Consequences:

- The new `ActivityComponent` entries in each `ReactTypeOfWork` map (including the `-1` "doesn't exist yet" values) and the new `ActivityComponent` field in `WorkTagMap` are effectively dead — nothing reads them.
- For inspected renderers where tag 31 is absent or has a different meaning (React <= 19.1, or a third-party renderer whose version string falls into the `gt(version, '17.0.1')` branch but has its own tag numbering), a non-Activity fiber would be mislabeled as `Activity` and wrongly filtered out of the DevTools tree.
- It also breaks the file's stated contract ("Keep it in sync, and add version guards if it changes"), so a future tag renumbering in `ReactWorkTags.js` would silently change DevTools behavior for all versions at once.

Please drop this import and instead read the tag from the version map: add `ActivityComponent` to the destructuring list inside `getInternalReactConstants` and to the destructuring list inside `attach`, so both switches use the version-appropriate value (`-1` on versions that don't have the tag, which can never match a real fiber).

comments.content: Unlike `createFiberFromOffscreen` / `createFiberFromLegacyHidden`, this factory intentionally does not attach an `OffscreenInstance` to `fiber.stateNode` (the internal Offscreen child created in `updateActivityComponent` owns it). This difference from the neighboring factories is easy to misread as an oversight, so a short comment noting the intent would help future maintainers.

The `ref`/`child`/`return` wiring plus the `return primaryChildFragment` is duplicated verbatim in the mount and update branches. Consider creating `primaryChildFragment` from either branch and doing the shared wiring once after the `if/else` to avoid the two copies drifting apart.

`updateActivityComponent` has no comment describing its non-obvious contract, and the local `mode` name is ambiguous: `nextMode` is an Offscreen mode string (`'visible' | 'hidden' | 'manual'`), while `mode` here is the `TypeOfMode` bitmask. Given the neighboring `updateOffscreenComponent` uses `mode` to mean the prop, this is easy to misread. A short comment explaining that Activity is a thin wrapper that always renders a single internal Offscreen fiber (which owns the `OffscreenInstance`/visibility state) — which is why the ref is forwarded to the child — plus renaming the bitmask would help future readers.
